#basic formatting 

This is **bold,** (that's double asterisks).Or *italics*. Or `code`. 

-this is the start of a list. 
-next item.
-next item.make sure to have space at the end of item. 

1. this is a numbered list. 
2. second item. 

To add a hyperlink,do`[link text](url)`. 
For Example,[go here](https://www.sewanee.edu)

To link to sections of your documents,do'[link text](#section-name)',without backticks.For example,[go here](#markdown).

Without back ticks,with hyphens for spaces, and everything lowercase 


To add more vertical space between blocks of text, use this:"&nbsp,"without quotes 

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

#Rmarkdown 
'RMarkdown' is just 'Markdown' with 'R' code woven in. 


You can R stuff in the same line as a text, for example,'r 3+3' will show as 6. (It would like backtick lower-case-rspace then code.then backtick).


You can also do a full-multi-line CHUNK of R stuff:  


{r,eval=false}

-`eval=True`:which acually runs the code if `FALSE`, it shows the code buy doesn't run it 
-`echo=TRUE': which shows the code, if `FALSE`, the code can run without being seen. 
-`warnings=FALSE`:which will turn off warnings.

- `fig.cap = "figure caption"` adds a figure caption. 

- `fig.width = 7` example of figure width. 

- `fig.height = 4` example of figure width. 

#Bringing in real data 
To manually set working directory while building up my Rmarkdown file, just go to 
Session> Set working directory > Source file location 


```{r read data, }
library(readr)
energy<-read_csv("../../data/IRENA data.csv",skip=1)

```

```{r explore data,} 
library(dplyr)
energy %>% names
energy %>% head 
energy %>% tail
energy %>% pull(Technology) %>% unique %>%sort 
energy %>% pull(`Country/area`)%>% unique 

```
